checklist.intro: The checklist below lists the minimum information that would have allowed every eligible data set in this atlas to be re-analysed and graded without manual curation, together with how often each item is currently recorded in GEO (series descriptions and sample annotations of the 518 discovery series and 1,088 contrasts curated here). Rates for clock time, feeding state and batch come from a keyword search of GEO text and are approximate.
rows: Population
Species, strain or genetic background, sex and age of every sample
Sex and age moderate exercise responses; only 31% of study clusters included females
Sex unreported in 30% and age in 28% of study clusters
Population
Health context or disease model, and training status at baseline
In liver, none of the 28 graded training genes remained graded when the analysis was restricted to healthy contexts
Not assessed
Exercise
Modality, relative intensity, session duration, frequency and total training length
In muscle, species shaped the training response more than training mode did
Modality unspecified or mixed in 8% of contrasts; training length missing for 21% of training contrasts
Exercise
Acute studies: time from the end of exercise to sampling
Responses change within hours: the blood response present at ≤1 h was gone by 12–72 h
Missing for 14% of acute contrasts (61/445)
Exercise
Training studies: time from the last bout to sampling
Acute effects of the last bout carried into 'training' samples are a candidate source of disagreement
Recorded for 10% of training contrasts (64/612)
Sampling
Clock time of sampling (and light–dark phase for rodents)
Clock and glucocorticoid-responsive genes were among the most heterogeneous genes in five of seven tissues
Annotated per sample in 2% of series (8/518); mentioned anywhere in 5%
Sampling
Feeding or fasting state at sampling
Feeding state alters metabolic transcripts and metabolites independently of exercise
Annotated per sample in 2% of series; mentioned anywhere in 10%
Sampling
Tissue, anatomical site or depot, and sampling procedure
Bulk tissue mixes regions and cell types; site-specific responses are diluted
Not assessed
Design
Group allocation and subject identifiers for repeated measures
Paired designs are far more powerful and must be analysed as such
Not assessed (contrasts without resolvable pairs were analysed as independent groups)
Design
Processing batches and how they were balanced or randomized across groups
16–30% of contrasts in training units showed genome-wide shifts, which group-aligned batches can produce
Batch annotated per sample in 4% of series
Data
Raw counts or intensities for every sample, not only normalized or group-level tables
Uniform re-processing requires per-sample raw data
Uniform counts available for 64% of re-analysed RNA-seq contrasts; 134 needed manual column mapping; 88 eligible contrasts were unusable
Data
Machine-readable sample annotations linking each sample to group, time point, subject and batch
Contrast definitions in this atlas required reading free text for every series
Not assessed
Data
Analysis code, software versions and the full differential-analysis output
Allows effect sizes to be recomputed and compared
Not assessed
